subject: POC: performance-tied pricing vs. flat top-up — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@cloudalpha.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for running the initial evaluation last week — the engineering team was impressed with Redwood's latency and the KV cache behaviour. We have just one blocker on our side: the analytics team needs two more weeks of live workload to validate the reranking quality at scale.

Before we ask procurement for extra spend, wanted to check whether you all would consider one of these approaches so we can get a clean extension without a long contract negotiation: 

- Short top-up: 2-week run extension charged at list rate but with a 20% credit if we hit SLO-derived success gates (latency < 120ms p50 and rerank auc delta <= 0.02).
- Performance fee: Redwood invoices an additional success fee (5% of POC spend) only if the model meets the production benchmarks by the end of the extension.

Either option avoids a long-term commitment which procurement prefers. Can you share which route you prefer and whether legal will need an addendum? Attaching the metrics matrix the team will use (POC_SLA_matrix.xlsx).

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Director, AI Platform
CloudAlpha

--- attachment: POC_SLA_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~12KB)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Alyssa — thanks for the clear asks and for the matrix. We're aligned that a short runway is reasonable so you can validate with live traffic. High level response:

- We can do the 2-week top-up with a conditional credit tied to the success gates you defined.
- Alternatively, we can structure a modest success fee — ben, can you sketch the commercial math?

Operational items: 
- Evelyn, can your team confirm the test harness and log scoping so we can verify the metrics independently?
- We will need a brief addendum that covers: extension dates, success gates, attribution window for metrics, and an acceptance signature. Legal usually accepts a 1-page addendum for this kind of PoC tweak.

Ben — loop in procurement pricing and whether we want to offer a small introductory discount on the top-up to keep the net spend neutral for CloudAlpha.

I'll propose language for the addendum once we agree on the commercial route.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Tessa / Alyssa — thanks. Quick commercial note with numbers so procurement can evaluate tradeoffs: 

Option A — 2-week top-up (list rate):
- List top-up: $8,000 (two weeks of equivalent POC capacity)
- Conditional credit: 20% ($1,600) refunded/credited if success gates met
- Effective if gates met: $6,400 net

Option B — Success fee model:
- Pay list for extension: $8,000
- If success gates met: 5% additional fee on total POC spend (est. $400), billed at acceptance
- Net if gates met: $8,400 (higher but aligns incentives)

Ben's recommendation: Offer Option A with a small one-time 10% introductory discount on the top-up (so list $8,000 -> $7,200) and keep the conditional 20% credit on acceptance. That gives CloudAlpha an attractive net while keeping our unit economics workable. 

Evelyn — operationally, we should confirm the attribution window (Alyssa suggested end-of-extension snapshot). Also want to avoid ambiguous metric definitions turning into disputes. Can we take ownership of the verification process?

Happy to run those numbers in the addendum.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Thanks all. A couple of operational clarifications to avoid edge cases: 

- Verification window: we will capture a 72-hour rolling window at the end of the extension for the rerank AUC delta and latency percentiles. That avoids transient noise.
- Baseline: we'll use the most recent daily baseline snapshot taken on 2027-04-19 as the reference for "delta".
- Logging: please ensure the request IDs are preserved and forwarded in your logs; we will ask for a minimum sample size of 10k inference requests for the acceptance test.

If CloudAlpha wants to include a third-party auditor for verification, we can accommodate that, but it will require an NDA addendum.

I'll draft the acceptance test section and include the exact metric calculation (AUC delta formula and p50 reporting). Attaching the draft term sheet we usually use for these addenda (redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

--- attachment: redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf (PDF, ~48KB)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, procure@cloudalpha.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Tessa / Ben / Evelyn — this looks good. Procurement reviewed Ben's numbers and prefers Option A with your recommended 10% introductory discount and the 20% success credit. They also want the acceptance window and verification mechanics documented in the addendum (fine).

Next steps from our side: 
- I will route the 2-week top-up approval through procurement this morning (procure@cloudalpha.com is on copy).
- Please send the 1-page addendum with the exact dates (proposed: 2027-04-23 through 2027-05-06), success gates language, and where the credit shows up on the invoice. We can sign electronically.

If you can get the addendum into DocuSign today, we'll aim to have it countersigned by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Director, AI Platform
CloudAlpha

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cloudalpha.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, procure@cloudalpha.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + performance incentive?

Great — I'll put the addendum together and route it through legal. Plan: 

- Addendum highlights: 2-week extension (2027-04-23 — 2027-05-06), top-up list $8,000 -> 10% intro discount -> $7,200 invoiced up front, conditional 20% credit ($1,600) applied on next invoice if acceptance gates met over the 72-hour verification window.
- Verification: Evelyn will verify using the 72-hour rolling window and the 2027-04-19 baseline snapshot; CloudAlpha will share request IDs for sampling.
- Signature: DocuSign link will include the redlined addendum; once countersigned we'll provision capacity in the IR cluster and tag the job.

I'll upload the addendum to DocuSign and paste the link here. Expect the DocuSign link in ~60–90 minutes.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting you the extra runway.

Best,
Tessa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
